title: Kahana vs Kajabi: Discovery Beside the LMS
excerpt: Kajabi is all-in-one creator business: courses, memberships, email, and landing pages for running a teaching brand end-to-end. Kahana is discovery + cohort discussion around teaching you already run elsewhere.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Founded in 2010; based in Newport Beach / Irvine, California.
Valued at >USD 2B after raising USD 550M growth financing.
Creators on Kajabi have collectively earned USD 9–10B+ in revenue from customers (2024–2025).
100,000+ creators and entrepreneurs use Kajabi, serving 150M+ customers; annual GMV through Kajabi creators exceeds USD 5B.

strengths.title: True all-in-one stack
strengths.detail: Website builder, courses, coaching, memberships, communities, email, funnels, analytics, and payments under one roof, fewer separate subscriptions.

strengths.title: Integrated business workflows
strengths.detail: Automations, landing pages, pipelines, and analytics designed to scale a knowledge business.

strengths.title: Single login for customers
strengths.detail: Students access courses, coaching, and community via one Kajabi account, better UX and loyalty.

strengths.title: Strong support and training
strengths.detail: Robust support, live chat, onboarding, expert community, and regular product updates.

weaknesses.title: High cost / pricing barrier
weaknesses.detail: Significantly more expensive than many competitors; often prohibitive for individuals or early-stage creators, cost is a top complaint even among fans.

weaknesses.title: Limited customization in places
weaknesses.detail: Templates look good, but deeper customization (payment pages, some funnel steps, advanced branding) can feel constrained.

weaknesses.title: Learning curve and complexity
weaknesses.detail: Breadth of features means a steeper learning curve; new or non-technical creators may struggle to use everything.

weaknesses.title: Bugs, performance, and mobile issues
weaknesses.detail: Occasional slow performance and bugs, especially on the mobile app and complex site builds.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Kajabi is all-in-one creator business: courses, memberships, email, and landing pages for running a teaching brand end-to-end. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Kajabi is an all-in-one platform that lets you create, market, and sell online courses and coaching programs, as well as other kinds of digital products, including your podcast.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Kajabi side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Kajabi you can use Courses, Memberships, Community & Messaging, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. You are running a full course engine: drip, quizzes, student progress, and checkout that already works.

Using Kahana with Kajabi

You can use both. Kajabi keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the course engine on Kajabi for drip, quizzes, and enrollment. Also list or link that teaching on Kahana so Explore, Clubs, and Aura can give it another place to be found. Kajabi stays the LMS; Kahana is another surface for exposure.
